CONSISTENCY RECORD: the eight-mark card in this chapter that asks for a full account of silicones closes on the uses, and names the SAME four: silicone rubbers; sealants, greases and electrical insulators; surgical and cosmetic implants; and the waterproofing of fabrics. TWO SUPPORTING REASONS ARE CARRIED BEYOND THE SOURCE LIST and should be confirmed by a teacher: that a silicone does not conduct electricity (the reason behind the insulator use) and that water does not wet a silicone surface (the reason behind the waterproofing use). Both are the standard explanations for these uses, and without them the answer is a bare list.

insider_note: The question asks for uses, so each line has to name a thing silicones are used AS or used FOR. A line that only names a property of silicones has not given a use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rubbers, sealants, greases and insulators
lines: Silicones are made into silicone rubbers.
They are also used as sealants, as
A silicone does not conduct electricity,
which is why insulating parts are made
steps.why: These four are all uses of a bulk silicone material — as a rubber, a sealant, a grease or an insulator — so they can be written as one short group.
common_mistakes: Giving a property in place of a use. Water repelling is a property; waterproofing a fabric is the use.
Naming a use of silica or of a silicate. This question is about silicones, the organosilicon polymers.
steps.memory_tip: Rubber, sealant, grease, insulator: four uses of the bulk silicone material.
steps.margin_note: Each use gets its own short sentence. Run together in one line they are hard to read back.

steps.label: Waterproofing and implants
lines: Fabrics are treated with silicones to
Silicones are also used in surgical and
Water does not wet a silicone surface, so
rain runs off a treated fabric.
steps.why: Both of these uses rest on the outward organic groups of the polymer. They give a surface that water does not wet, and a surface that stays unchanged in contact with living tissue.
common_mistakes: Saying the fabric itself repels water. The silicone coating on the fabric is the part water does not wet.
Leaving the medical use out. Silicones are used in surgical and cosmetic implants as well as in industry.
steps.memory_tip: Water does not wet a silicone, so silicones go on to fabrics and into implants.
steps.margin_note: Close by naming a use, not a property.
